Jeff Bezos built Amazon into a $200B+ empire.

And his most famous decision-making model was inspired by a book he has reread every year for 25+ years.

7 lessons from "The Remains of the Day":🧵 https://t.co/2GRqX4uoDe

The book follows Stevens, an English butler who sacrificed everything for "professional dignity."

But in his final years, he realizes a devastating truth:

• His dignity was a prison
• He never lived for himself
• His whole life was spent in fear https://t.co/V9AGxrqrtH

This revelation shook Bezos to his core.

At 30, he was the youngest Senior VP at D.E. Shaw:

• Making $1M/year
• On track to be partner
• Living the Wall Street dream

But something felt off: https://t.co/5R3Fzlp67y

That's when Bezos noticed internet usage growing 2,300% per year.

He faced a choice:

• Stay in his golden handcuffs
• Risk everything on the internet

The butler's story of regret haunted his decision. https://t.co/YGUm4S3anM

This led Bezos to create his famous "Regret Minimization Framework":

Imagine yourself at 80, looking back at life:

"Would you regret this decision?"

Here's how Bezos explains it: https://t.co/DcwssTSFP3

The answer became crystal clear.

Just like Stevens the butler, playing it safe was the riskiest move of all.

This insight became the foundation for 7 principles that would transform Amazon:

Lesson 1: Make decisions through the lens of your 80-year-old self

Most optimize for 2-3 years ahead.

But Bezos optimized for 40 years out:

• AWS took 10 years to profit
• Prime was mocked for years
• Kindle was called "Amazon's iPod of reading" https://t.co/4jrra6kJwA

Lesson 2: Professional dignity is a trap

Stevens wasted his life maintaining an image.

Bezos embraced being misunderstood:

• Left Wall Street at its peak
• Ignored quarterly profits
• Reinvested everything into growth https://t.co/LPsd21DrWJ

Lesson 3: Move with urgency and intensity

Stevens realized too late that time was his scarcest resource.

This birthed Amazon's "Day 1" philosophy:

• Make quick decisions
• High-velocity experimentation
• Never waste a day https://t.co/ohizI0UaKO

Lesson 4: Emotion drives the biggest breakthroughs

Bezos channeled emotion into:

• Customer obsession
• Long-term thinking
• Building trust

But Stevens suppressed his emotions, leading to regret. https://t.co/WasxXzqyyn

Then; list everything you need to do for your business (inputs). Allocate tasks into each day—try stick to themes.

Easy = SOPS. Templates. Swipe files etc. Remove all friction. Effective = Transform; reuse; systemise; improve quality.

1 minute extra effort; much better result. Repeat this for all your processes.
Then with things running smoothly… 𝟑. 𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐯𝐞
Ask: • Can I get a robot to do this? • Can I get someone else to do this?
AI/software first. VA second. Then train your VA to use the AI/software.
You don’t need a big team with this approach. We make $500k/year with just the two of us. And it’s getting easier and easier as we add more prompts.
Spend 2 hours a week on this stuff and by the end of the year you’ll have 100x output.
You don’t need to work harder. You need to work smarter. Systems are the secret.
